body:
Unfortunately, setting a refresh rate of 0 will cause https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104179 on some devices again, which is what we're trying to prevent here. We want the highest possible refresh rate so that the maximum FPS can be reached if there's no FPS limit.

My Galaxy S26 Ultra does not work this way for games at least (they can always reach 120 FPS), but as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104179 points out, other brands tend to cap to 60 Hz if the game doesn't explicitly request a higher refresh rate.

body:
Have we discussed if we want to preserve the pre-Android 14 behavior by default? 

The default approach we're taking is an automatic opt-in, as in regardless of the game / developer intent, we're aiming for the highest refresh rate if `application/run/max_fps` is not explicitly specified. By doing so, we may unnecessary cause more power consumption for games that have no desire to run beyond 60fps, which has an impact on store reviews / uninstall rates.

Another approach would be to require the game / developer to manually opt-in by specifying the desired target fps. Doing so would still address https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104179 as it would enable higher frame rates when explicitly specified.

body:
> Another approach would be to require the game / developer to manually opt-in by specifying the desired target fps.

This approach has some limits in terms of handling gaming phones with refresh rates above 120 Hz. Many developers would use a max FPS value of 120 (due to not knowing about these phones), which means games that *could* run at higher framerates won't do so. Keep in mind gaming phones have active cooling and large batteries, so it's usually no problem for them to run lightweight games at 144 or even 165 FPS.
